acute-angle: An angle that measures more than $0^\circ$ and less than $90^\circ$.
adjacent-angles: Two angles that share a vertex and one side, and do not overlap.
alternate-exterior-angles: Two angles outside the two lines, on opposite sides of the transversal. If the two lines are parallel, alternate exterior angles are equal.
alternate-interior-angles: Two angles between the two lines, on opposite sides of the transversal. If the two lines are parallel, alternate interior angles are equal.
angle: Two rays with the same endpoint. The endpoint is the vertex. Write $\angle ABC$, with the vertex in the middle.
angle-bisector: A ray that starts at the vertex of an angle and cuts the angle into two congruent angles.
area: The number of square units inside a figure.
bounding-box: The smallest rectangle with sides on grid lines that has a figure inside it. It is used to find area by subtracting the corner pieces.
collinear: Points that lie on the same line.
complementary: Two angles whose measures add to $90^\circ$. Each angle is the complement of the other.
congruent: Having the same size and shape. Congruent segments have the same length. Congruent angles have the same measure. The symbol is $\cong$.
converse: The statement you get by turning an “if, then” rule around.
convex-polygon: A polygon where every segment between two points of the polygon stays inside it. A polygon that is not convex is concave. A concave polygon has a corner that points inward.
coordinate-plane: A flat surface with a horizontal $x$-axis and a vertical $y$-axis. Every point has an ordered pair $(x, y)$.
coordinate-proof: A way to show a fact for sure by using coordinates, slopes, and distances instead of a picture. Also called computation as proof.
coplanar: Points or lines that lie in the same plane.
corresponding-angles: Two angles in the same position at the two places where a transversal crosses two lines. If the two lines are parallel, corresponding angles are equal.
degree: The unit for measuring angles, written $^\circ$. A full turn is $360^\circ$. A right angle is $90^\circ$.
diagonal: A segment that joins two corners of a polygon that are not next to each other.
distance-formula: The distance between $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$ is $d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}$.
endpoint: A point at the end of a segment or the start of a ray.
equiangular: Having all angles the same measure. An equiangular triangle has three $60^\circ$ angles.
equilateral-triangle: A triangle with all three sides the same length. Each angle measures $60^\circ$.
exterior-angle: An angle outside a polygon, made by one side and the extension of the next side. An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.
hypotenuse: The side of a right triangle across from the right angle. It is the longest side.
intersect: To cross or meet. Two lines intersect at a point. Two planes intersect in a line.
isosceles-triangle: A triangle with at least two sides the same length. The angles across from the equal sides are equal.
leg: One of the two sides of a right triangle that form the right angle.
like-radicals: Radicals with the same radicand. You can add them: $3\sqrt{2} + 5\sqrt{2} = 8\sqrt{2}$.
line: A straight path of points that goes on forever in both directions. Write $\overleftrightarrow{AB}$ or name it with one small letter, like line $\ell$.
linear-pair: Two adjacent angles whose outside sides are opposite rays. The angles in a linear pair are supplementary.
measure-of-an-angle: How far an angle opens, in degrees. Write $m\angle ABC = 40^\circ$. Read it as “the measure of angle $ABC$ is 40 degrees.”
midpoint: The point exactly halfway between the endpoints of a segment. It cuts the segment into two congruent segments.
obtuse-angle: An angle that measures more than $90^\circ$ and less than $180^\circ$.
opposite-rays: Two rays with the same endpoint that go in opposite directions. Together they make a line.
opposite-reciprocal: The number you get by flipping a fraction and changing its sign. Slopes of perpendicular lines are opposite reciprocals.
parallel: Parallel lines are in the same plane and never meet. They stay the same distance apart. The symbol is $\parallel$. In a figure, matching arrows mark parallel lines.
parallelogram: A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
partition: To divide a segment into parts. A point partitions a segment in the ratio $a:b$ when the two parts have lengths in the ratio $a$ to $b$.
perfect-square: A number that is the square of a whole number, such as 1, 4, 9, 16, 25.
perimeter: The distance around a polygon. It is the sum of the side lengths.
perpendicular: Perpendicular lines cross to make right angles. The symbol is $\perp$.
plane: A flat surface that goes on forever in every direction. Name it with one capital letter, like plane $P$, or with three points in it that are not on one line.
point: An exact location. A point has no size. Name it with a capital letter, like point $A$.
polygon: A closed figure made of three or more segments, called sides, that meet only at their endpoints. A polygon with $n$ sides is an $n$-gon. The angles of a polygon with $n$ sides add to $(n - 2) \cdot 180^\circ$.
protractor: A tool that measures angles in degrees. It has an outer scale and an inner scale. Read the scale that starts at $0$ on one side of the angle.
pythagorean-theorem: In a right triangle, the sum of the squares of the legs equals the square of the hypotenuse: $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$.
pythagorean-triple: Three whole numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ with $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$.
radical: An expression with a root sign, such as $\sqrt{50}$ or $3\sqrt{2}$. The number under the sign is the radicand.
radicand: The number under a radical sign. In $\sqrt{50}$ the radicand is 50.
rationalize: To rewrite a fraction so that the denominator has no radical.
ray: Part of a line that starts at one endpoint and goes on forever in one direction. Write $\overrightarrow{AB}$: it starts at $A$ and goes through $B$.
rectangle: A parallelogram with a right angle.
regular-polygon: A polygon with all sides the same length and all angles the same measure.
rhombus: A quadrilateral with four sides of equal length.
right-angle: An angle that measures exactly $90^\circ$. A small square at the vertex marks a right angle.
same-side-interior-angles: Two angles between the two lines, on the same side of the transversal. If the two lines are parallel, same-side interior angles are supplementary.
scalene-triangle: A triangle with no two sides the same length.
segment: Part of a line between two endpoints. Write $\overline{AB}$. Its length is written $AB$, with no bar.
segment-bisector: A point, line, ray, or segment that goes through the midpoint of a segment.
skew: Skew lines are not in the same plane. They do not meet and they are not parallel.
slope: A number that tells how steep a line is: the change in $y$ divided by the change in $x$, or rise over run.
square: A quadrilateral that is both a rectangle and a rhombus: four equal sides and four right angles.
square-root: A number that gives the original number when you multiply it by itself. In geometry we use the positive root.
straight-angle: An angle that measures exactly $180^\circ$. Its sides are opposite rays, so it looks like a line.
supplementary: Two angles whose measures add to $180^\circ$. Each angle is the supplement of the other.
transversal: A line that crosses two or more other lines at different points.
triangle: A polygon with three sides and three angles. The angles of a triangle add to $180^\circ$. Write $\triangle ABC$.
triangle-inequality: The two shorter sides of a triangle always add to more than the longest side.
vertex: The point where the two sides of an angle meet. The plural is vertices.
vertical-angles: The two angles across from each other when two lines cross. Vertical angles are equal.
